subject: Clarify auto-renewal notice & termination for convenience — MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmeenergy.com>
To: rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reddick <tom@acmeenergy.com>, legal@acmeenergy.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on renewal/termination language for Redwood MSA + Order Form

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the draft Order Form and MSA. Our legal team had a few targeted questions before we move this to signature related to term and termination mechanics:

- Auto-renew: the Order Form currently says the Term auto-renews for successive 1-year periods unless either party gives notice "prior to the end of the then-current Term." Can you confirm what the required notice window is? We prefer a 60-day notice but would like to understand Redwood's flexibility.

- Termination for convenience: the MSA has a termination-for-convenience right but no explicit payment/closeout requirements. Our procurement asks that there be a clear obligation for a pro-rated refund or fees for committed capacity if we terminate early, or alternatively a 60-day notice plus payment of committed run-rate for that period.

- Order Form tie-in: please confirm whether an Order Form without a signed amendment can be non-renewing while the MSA auto-renews. We want to avoid mismatched auto-renew cycles.

Can you loop in your contracts/legal and propose clean language we can review? We have a target procurement approval by 3/22.

Thanks,
Samantha

--

Head of Procurement
Acme Energy

Subject: Re: Questions on renewal/termination language for Redwood MSA + Order Form

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (sales ops) to propose contract language and confirm operational impact.

Internal note to Marissa/Karthik/Lauren: see Acme's asks below. Quick commercial context — Acme is asking for 60-day auto-renew notice and a termination-for-convenience mechanics that provides either pro-rated refund or a short pay-through. They're a mid-market energy customer; we want to keep flexibility but avoid long tail financial exposure from reserved capacity.

My suggested starting positions:
- Auto-renew notice: agree to 60 days instead of our standard "prior to the end of the then-current Term" (which is operationally 30 days). 60 days is reasonable for their procurement timelines.
- Termination for convenience: propose 60 days' notice with an obligation to pay for the remainder of the 60-day notice period (no longer-term committed buyouts). For order forms with prepaid reserved capacity, allow pro-rata refund for unused prepaid months net of any usage-based charges.
- Order Form/MSA tie: clarify that Order Forms inherit the MSA term and renewals unless an Order Form specifically lists an explicit non-renewing end date. That avoids mismatches.

Marissa — can you draft redline snippets for the MSA (Sections 2.1 Term; 2.3 Renewal; 9.2 Termination for Convenience) and a short paragraph to add to the Order Form template describing how it ties to MSA term? We'd like to get a redline over to Acme by EOD today if possible.

Thanks,
Rohan

Subject: Re: Questions on renewal/termination language for Redwood MSA + Order Form

Thanks Rohan — drafting redlines now. High-level legal trade-offs and proposed language below. I'll attach a redlined PDF and a clean replacement paragraph for the Order Form.

Key points I considered:
- Notice window: 60 days is acceptable; it reduces churn risk and gives both parties time to transition. We'll convert references generally to "sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Term."
- Termination for convenience: acceptable with a 60-day notice. To protect Redwood financially when reserved capacity is involved, propose the following closeout mechanics: if Customer terminates for convenience, Customer will (a) pay for charges incurred through the date of termination; (b) if Customer has prepaid reserved capacity, Redwood will refund any unused prepaid amounts pro rata, less any usage-based fees and any reasonable early-termination administration charge not to exceed an agreed cap (e.g., $25,000). Alternatively, Customer can elect to continue access for the 60-day notice period and pay the recurring fees instead of receiving a refund.
- Order Form tie-in: recommend a short clause in the Order Form: "Unless an Order Form specifies otherwise, the Term and renewal mechanics in the MSA govern the Services ordered under the Order Form." This prevents contradictory renewals.

Proposed MSA snippets (for redline):
- Section 2.1 (Term): "The Initial Term of this Agreement will begin on the Effective Date and continue for the period set forth in the applicable Order Form. Thereafter, the Agreement will automatically renew for successive one (1) year periods unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Term."

- Section 9.2 (Termination for Convenience): "Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other Party. If Customer terminates for convenience, Customer shall (i) pay all Fees accrued through the date of termination, and (ii) receive a pro rata refund of any pre-paid, unused fees for Services not delivered as of the effective date of termination, less (A) any usage-based charges incurred and (B) an early termination administration fee not to exceed twenty-five thousand dollars (USD 25,000), unless otherwise agreed in the applicable Order Form. Alternatively, Customer may elect to continue to receive Services during the sixty (60) day notice period and shall remain responsible for all recurring Fees during such period."

- Order Form paragraph: "Term and Renewal: The Term for Services ordered under an Order Form shall be as specified therein. Unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise, such Order Form shall be subject to the Term and renewal provisions of the MSA, including any required notice periods for non-renewal."

I'll attach the PDFs now (Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.pdf; OrderForm_Acme_v2.docx). If Sales wants a commercial alternative (e.g., commit buyout equal to remaining 3 months rather than pro-rata refund), let me know and I can mark up options.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Questions on renewal/termination language for Redwood MSA + Order Form

Hi Samantha — thanks for the patience. Attached is a redline (Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.pdf) and an updated Order Form (OrderForm_Acme_v2.docx) with the language Marissa proposed. Key points:

1) Auto-renewal notice: we updated the MSA to require sixty (60) days' prior written notice for non-renewal.
2) Termination for convenience: either party may give 60 days' notice. If Acme terminates for convenience, you can either take a pro-rata refund for unused prepaid reserved capacity (less usage and a capped admin fee) or elect to continue service through the 60-day notice and pay the recurring fees.
3) Order Forms: by default an Order Form inherits the MSA Term and renewal mechanics unless it expressly states otherwise.

Next steps: can you confirm by close of business 3/18 whether Acme accepts the redlines as-is, would like the alternative commercial option (short buyout equal to remaining 3 months), or wants us to schedule a quick 30-minute call to talk through trade-offs? If accepted, we'll issue a final clean copy for signature and send a DocuSign link.

Thanks — look forward to closing this out.

Best,
Rohan
